decks.name: LeetCode #104 - Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
decks.description: Find the maximum depth of a binary tree from root to furthest leaf

cards.question: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth. A binary tree's maximum depth is the number of nodes along the longest path from the root node down to the farthest leaf node.

solutions.name: Recursive DFS
solutions.explanation: Use recursive depth-first search to compute tree height. Base case returns 0 for null nodes. For each node, recursively compute depth of left and right subtrees, return 1 plus maximum of the two. Clean recursive solution with space proportional to tree height for call stack.

Recursively call maxDepth with root dot left and maxDepth with root dot right, take max of results, add one for current node, and return.

solutions.timeDescription: Linear time as each node is visited exactly once during depth-first traversal
solutions.spaceDescription: Recursion stack space proportional to tree height h, O(log n) for balanced tree, O(n) worst case for skewed tree
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given tree [3,9,20,null,null,15,7]: maxDepth(3): max(maxDepth(9), maxDepth(20)). maxDepth(9): max(0,0)=0, return 1. maxDepth(20): max(maxDepth(15), maxDepth(7)). maxDepth(15)=1, maxDepth(7)=1, max=1, return 2. maxDepth(3): max(1,2)=2, return 3.

solutions.name: Breadth First Search
solutions.explanation: Use BFS with queue to traverse tree level by level. Initialize level counter to 0. For each level, process all nodes at current level, add children to queue, then increment level. When queue empty, level count equals maximum depth. Natural approach for computing tree depth by counting levels.
